finding: grunberg_nissan_mix has exactly 1 production call site(s) in the entire crate (src/lib.rs, inside theory_apparent_viscosity), and it and both of the function's own unit tests supply ONLY a hardcoded all-zero interaction matrix. No struct field anywhere in the module schema (RheologyObservationV1, LiquidComponentV1, PigmentComponentV1, RheologyAdditiveV1) carries interaction-parameter data, so even a caller with real Grunberg-Nissan d_ij data has no way to supply it. theory_apparent_viscosity is called by both fit_model (line 1334, 1473 in src/lib.rs) and predict, i.e. every training row and every scored candidate. An independent pure-Python re-derivation confirms the live-Rust zero-interaction result is bit-equivalent (within 1e-9) to plain ideal (mass-fraction-weighted log-linear) mixing, and that supplying a non-zero, order-unity interaction term (the term that defines Grunberg-Nissan over ideal mixing) changes the result by 28.4% -- proving the omitted term is not negligible when the function IS given real interaction data. The module's cited "Grunberg-Nissan blend mixing" built-in path (docs/mission.md; reference/rheology/source-landscape.v1.json source_id "grunberg-nissan-1949") is, as actually wired into the live runtime, architecturally incapable of ever computing anything other than ideal mixing -- this is a structural/architecture gap, not merely a data gap awaiting wet-lab validation as mission.md currently frames it alongside Krieger-Dougherty and Herschel-Bulkley.
